questions.q: What is the main inefficiency of full-range liquidity (the model from Lessons 5-8)?
options: Most of an LP's capital sits at price levels that will realistically never be reached, earning zero fees while still deployed
It charges LPs a higher trading fee than concentrated pools
It cannot accept deposits from more than one LP at a time
It requires LPs to actively manage their position every day
questions.explain: Full-range liquidity spreads capital across the entire 0-to-infinity price curve, even though a pair usually trades in a narrow band, leaving most capital idle.

questions.q: What does a concentrated liquidity position let an LP do differently from a full-range position?
options: Avoid paying any trading fees to the protocol
Deposit only within a chosen price range instead of the entire price curve
Guarantee a fixed interest rate regardless of trading activity
Eliminate impermanent loss entirely
questions.explain: Concentrated liquidity (introduced by Uniswap v3) lets an LP pick a specific price range and deposit only within it, rather than across the full curve.

questions.q: Per the worked example, roughly how much less capital can a concentrated LP use to provide the same fee-earning depth near the current price as a full-range LP?
options: About 2x less
Exactly the same amount of capital is required either way
Roughly 10-20x less
About 100,000x less
questions.explain: Because a full-range LP has only ~1-2% of capital actively near the current price, a concentrated LP can match that depth using roughly 10-20x less total capital.

questions.q: What happens to a concentrated liquidity position when the price moves entirely outside its chosen range?
options: Nothing changes — it continues earning fees exactly as before
The LP's funds are automatically returned to their wallet
The protocol automatically widens the range for the LP
The position converts entirely into whichever asset is now cheaper, and stops earning fees until price re-enters the range
questions.explain: Once price exits the chosen range, the position holds only the cheaper asset and earns no fees until price moves back inside the range.

questions.q: What are "ticks" in a concentrated-liquidity pool?
options: Discrete price boundaries that define the edges of a liquidity position
A unit of trading fee revenue
A measurement of a token's total supply
The name for an LP token in Uniswap v3
questions.explain: A position is defined by a lower and upper tick, and its liquidity only counts toward swap pricing (is "active") while the current price sits between those ticks.
